newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-VALENCIA FINALLY OFF THE MARK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VALENCIA FINALLY OFF THE MARK.

text.p: Troubled Valencia gained their first Spanish league point of the season in a 1-1 draw with Zaragoza on Saturday but the match was overshadowed by a rash of bookings and a sending off.

Zaragoza came out strongly and took the lead through Xavier Aguado in the 11th minute. But they fell apart after the 27th minute departure of forward Santiago Aragon. He was sent off in unclear circumstances shortly after falling in the Valencia area.
After the game Aragon denied insulting the referee for rejecting his penalty appeal.
The rest of the first half yielded six bookings, as the match official -- who was making his first division debut -- seemed to lose control.
Valencia's Gabriel Moya put Valencia level just before the break after pouncing on a rebound from his own header.
After a brief lull in the second half, the spate of fouls continued, and several players were lucky to stay on the pitch.
Valencia had the better of the play, but were unable to make the most of their numerical advantage.

They beat UEFA Cup holders Bayern Munich 3-0 on Tuesday, but had seen their match preparations disrupted by a new clash between coach Luis Aragones and Brazilian forward Romario, who has been dropped.
